ui.tagline: The all-round Studio — image and video models, content tools, and code.
ui.description: The general-purpose workspace most bots should use. Includes Claude Code, AI Gen, the Skills CLI, a TypeScript toolchain, and all three Node package managers. Pick this when you don't need anything beyond standard web/Node/AI tooling.

@anthropic-ai/claude-code.blurb: Anthropic's coding assistant runs right inside the workspace.

packs.description: Python 3 + pip + venv + build tooling for native extensions.
packs.agentGuidance: Python 3 is at `python3` (no unversioned `python`). Use `pip3 install --break-system-packages <pkg>` for system-wide installs (this image follows PEP 668), or `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` for a project-local venv. Native-extension build tools (build-essential, pkg-config, python3-dev) are present, so packages like Pillow, lxml, manim can compile from source if needed.

packs.description: FFmpeg for video/audio encoding and frame-to-MP4 assembly.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `ffmpeg -i <input> <output>` for transcoding, `ffmpeg -framerate <fps> -i frame_%04d.png out.mp4` for frame sequences, and `ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>` to inspect media. The Debian ffmpeg build includes the common codecs (libx264, libvpx, aac); use `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for broadly-compatible MP4 output.

packs.description: TeX Live (LaTeX) + dvisvgm — needed for MathTex / Tex rendering in animation pipelines and for PDF/SVG math output.
packs.agentGuidance: Compile LaTeX with `pdflatex <file.tex>` or `latex <file.tex>`. The texlive-latex-extra, texlive-fonts-extra, texlive-latex-recommended, texlive-science and tipa packages are included — covering Manim's `MathTex`/`Tex` requirements and most paper-style documents. Use `dvisvgm <file.dvi>` to convert DVI to SVG. First invocation is slow (font cache build); subsequent calls are fast.

packs.description: Xvfb virtual framebuffer + Mesa OpenGL libs — lets headless OpenGL workloads (ManimGL, Blender headless, etc.) render without a real display.
packs.agentGuidance: Wrap OpenGL/GUI commands with `xvfb-run -a <command>` to give them a virtual display (`-a` auto-picks a free server number). For longer pipelines export a persistent display: `Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 & export DISPLAY=:99`. Required for ManimGL (`manimgl`); not required for Manim CE (`manim`) which renders headlessly via Cairo.

packs.description: Manim Community Edition (manim) + ManimGL (manimlib) — the two leading Python animation engines, with their native Cairo/Pango deps.
packs.agentGuidance: Two engines coexist. Manim CE — `manim -ql <file.py> <SceneClass>` (Cairo-based, headless, default for most agents). ManimGL — `xvfb-run -a manimgl <file.py> <SceneClass>` (OpenGL; the import itself opens a display, so any `manimgl` invocation or even `import manimlib` must be wrapped in `xvfb-run -a` or run with `DISPLAY` set — the xvfb pack provides this). Python import names differ: `import manim` vs `import manimlib`. Renders land in `./media/videos/<file>/<quality>/<SceneClass>.mp4` by default; pass `--media_dir /home/user/artifacts` to redirect into the artifacts mount. Use `-ql` (480p), `-qm` (720p), `-qh` (1080p) to trade speed for quality.

packs.description: Shared system libraries required to run a headless Chrome / Chrome Headless Shell on Debian Bookworm. Installs no browser binary — downstream packs (e.g. remotion) fetch their own Chrome.
packs.agentGuidance: Provides the native shared libraries a headless Chromium needs (NSS, GBM/Mesa, ALSA, ATK + ATK-bridge, Cairo/Pango, X composite/damage/fixes/randr, CUPS, dbus). It installs NO browser binary — tools that drive headless Chrome (Remotion, Puppeteer, Playwright) must download or point at their own Chromium build; this pack only guarantees the OS-level .so dependencies resolve. If a render fails with `error while loading shared libraries: libXXX.so: cannot open shared object file`, the missing library belongs here.

packs.description: Remotion CLI (React/HTML → MP4 video rendering) with a Chrome Headless Shell pre-downloaded at build time and exposed at a fixed, world-readable path so the non-root runtime user can render offline.
packs.agentGuidance: Remotion renders React compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome. The CLI is installed globally (`remotion`). A Chrome Headless Shell is pre-downloaded to the fixed, world-readable path /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell (also exported as $CHROME_HEADLESS_SHELL in interactive shells), so renders work offline without the ~150MB first-run download. Remotion has NO env var for the browser path, so you MUST pass it explicitly with the literal path (env vars are not present in non-interactive `commands.run`): `remotion render <entry> <CompositionId> /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --browser-executable /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell`. Typical flow: scaffold or open a Remotion project (`package.json` with `remotion` + `src/index.ts` calling registerRoot, and a Root that registers <Composition> ids), `npm install`, then render with the flag above. Without `--browser-executable`, Remotion re-downloads Chrome into the project's node_modules/.remotion. System ffmpeg is present (the ffmpeg pack); Remotion also bundles its own. Domain knowledge lives in the `remotion-best-practices` skill (`skills add remotion-best-practices`) — 38 rule files on captions, audio, sequencing, transitions, fonts, etc.

packs.description: HeyGen HyperFrames CLI (HTML/CSS/GSAP → deterministic MP4 via headless Chrome + ffmpeg). Requires Node 22+. Ships the 0.8.x CLI generation: `check` remains the unified verification gate (lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/contrast audit in one pass), the lint rule set is materially quieter than 0.7.x (0.8.5–0.8.8 dropped eleven rules that fired on correct compositions), and a caught post-render throw no longer reports a valid render as failed. A PINNED Chrome is pre-installed and its path is frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path (+ /opt/chrome/chrome symlink) so renders run offline with no per-run download. Local-only/keyless render core: voiceover/captions/background-removal are produced via AI Gen (not bundled local weights); HeyGen cloud features and @hyperframes/aws-lambda are excluded — which is why 0.8.0's cloud-transport migration boundary (Lambda/SAM/CDK and Cloud Run redeploy) does not apply to this image.
packs.agentGuidance: HeyGen HyperFrames renders HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome (Puppeteer beginFrame seeking) + ffmpeg. The CLI is global (`hyperframes`). Flow: `hyperframes init --non-interactive` to scaffold, edit the composition + animation tracks, verify with `hyperframes check` (the canonical gate: lint + headless-browser runtime/layout/motion/WCAG audit; exit 0 required), then `hyperframes render --output /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --non-interactive`. CHROME (pinned, offline): a pinned Chrome is pre-staged; its absolute path is frozen at /etc/sl8/chrome-path and as the /opt/chrome/chrome symlink. `hyperframes doctor` auto-detects it; if a command needs it explicitly, pass `--chrome "$(cat /etc/sl8/chrome-path)"`. Do NOT trigger a Puppeteer/Chrome download and do NOT rely on image ENV (E2B `commands.run` does not inherit it). GSAP: vendor GSAP into the composition — do not depend on a render-time CDN fetch (cdn.jsdelivr.net). FONTS / OFFLINE CLOSURE (the render-time network is closed; a composition that reaches for a font at compile time is the most common way to break a sandbox render): (1) strip every `` to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com and every `@import` of a remote stylesheet; (2) map each family you want to one already packed in the image — list them with `fc-list : family | sort -u`; (3) declare it with `@font-face { font-family: ''; src: local(''); }` INSIDE the composition wrapper, not in a sibling stylesheet, so the compiler inlines it; (4) verify by running the compile and confirming zero outbound font fetches, then `hyperframes check` exit 0. Never let the compiler resolve a family by name alone and never rely on a network retry — 0.8.x surfaces that failure as FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, which in a closed sandbox means a failed render, not a slow one. MEDIA (voiceover/captions/background-removal are NOT local — use AI Gen, keyless via the SL8 proxy): voiceover → `ai-gen audio tts "" -m fal-ai/kokoro/american-english`; captions/timing → `ai-gen transcribe

packs.description: Curated font set for caption/composition rendering: DejaVu family (Sans, Sans Oblique, Serif Italic at guaranteed paths) + Comic Neue (OFL casual), plus an embeddable OFL webfont pack (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) for legible, consistent HyperFrames/video compositions. fontconfig (fc-list/fc-match) for discovery.
packs.agentGuidance: Fonts are pre-installed — do NOT probe the filesystem or fetch fonts at runtime. Guaranteed TTF paths for ffmpeg drawtext fontfile=: /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (clean sans, default), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf (sans oblique), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif-Italic.ttf (serif italic). Casual/handwriting: Comic Neue (OFL; resolve with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Comic Neue'`). Embeddable webfonts for compositions (HyperFrames HTML/CSS or ffmpeg drawtext font='...'): Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk — installed under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/sl8-webfonts and registered with fontconfig, so reference by family name (e.g. `font='Inter'`) or resolve a file with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Outfit'`. `fc-list` enumerates everything installed. ffmpeg's drawtext is built with fontconfig, so family names work as an alternative to fontfile=.

ui.tagline: Adds Python, Manim, Remotion, HyperFrames, ffmpeg, and LaTeX on top of General.
ui.description: Everything in General, plus a full code-to-video stack: Python 3.11, Manim Community Edition + ManimGL, Remotion (React/HTML → MP4), HeyGen HyperFrames (HTML/CSS → MP4), ffmpeg, TeX Live, and Xvfb for headless GL rendering. Runs on Node 22. Use this when your bot needs to render math/diagram animations or programmatic web video.

manim.blurb: Render math and diagram animations as MP4.

remotion.blurb: Render React/HTML compositions to MP4 (Chrome Headless Shell pre-installed).

hyperframes.blurb: HeyGen HyperFrames — render HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4 (pinned Chrome at /etc/sl8/chrome-path, Pillow; voiceover/captions/background-removal via ai-gen; Node 22).

fonts.blurb: Embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) plus DejaVu/Comic-Neue for legible compositions.

chrome-headless.blurb: Headless-Chrome system libraries that browser-based renderers depend on.

ffmpeg.blurb: Encode and convert video and audio.

packs.description: Bakes the hyperframes-studio skill suite (locked registry pins, incl. the 5-skill motion-quality DOCTRINE chain) into /home/user/.claude/skills and pre-warms the npx cache for the project-pinned hyperframes CLI — the studio template rule: sessions never re-install what every session needs. Suite source of truth: studio/hyperframes-studio/releases/vN/suite.lock.json; refresh = new template version. Requires a GITHUB_TOKEN build env (registry read); blanked from the image ENV after install.
packs.agentGuidance: The studio skill suite is PRE-INSTALLED at /home/user/.claude/skills (the /hyperframes router, the motion-graphics workflow, 9 domain skills incl. hyperframes-audio, AND the 5-skill motion-quality doctrine chain: motion-doctrine — load it FIRST for any motion work, its rules supersede generic motion guidance — plus cut-the-curve, seam-craft, oversized-cursor, captions-overlay). Do NOT reinstall; start every video/motion request at the /hyperframes router. STEP DISCIPLINE (non-negotiable): follow the routed workflow's numbered steps exactly — DISPATCH the workflow's sub-agents where the runbook says dispatch (e.g. motion-graphics: Director Part 1 → source → Director Part 2 → Builder → verify, each a Task dispatch), leave every step's artifact on disk (shot-plan.json, compositions/index.html, snapshots/contact-sheet.jpg), and run the snapshot proof BEFORE render. Autonomous mode means checkpoint summaries, never skipped steps. PROJECT ROOT: map the workflow's PROJECT_DIR under /home/user/artifacts/<project>/ (one folder per project). Other workflow skills install lazily on route (`skills add <workflow>`, needs GITHUB_TOKEN). The hyperframes CLI npx cache is pre-warmed: render via the project-pinned form (`npx --yes hyperframes@<pinned> render ...`). OFFLINE CLOSURE: strip Google Fonts links (0.8.x still auto-fetches; a closed sandbox turns that into FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, i.e. a FAILED render), map families to the packed fonts (Inter/Outfit/Fraunces/Anton/Space Grotesk), declare `@font-face { src: local('X') }` INSIDE each composition's [data-composition-id] wrapper; closure oracle = `check` exit 0 with zero 'Fetched ... from Google Fonts' compiler lines. AUDIO: mixing already-placed audio (fades, crossfade, gain, ducking, voiceover carve, FX, automation envelopes) is `hyperframes-audio` — new at the 0.8.8 refresh; sourcing or generating audio remains media-use.

ui.tagline: Motion graphics and generative animation — programmatic motion for Specialists who make things move.
ui.description: The HyperFrames studio, ready to work: the full skill suite is pre-installed (the /hyperframes router, motion-graphics workflow, and 8 domain skills for animation, keyframes, creative direction, media, and Figma import), the HyperFrames 0.7.x renderer and a pinned offline Chrome are baked, and fonts, ffmpeg, and Python ship in the image. Give it a one-line idea, a product URL, or a document — it plans, designs, animates, verifies with the built-in check gate, and renders a production MP4. More workflows (explainers, launches, slideshows, captions) install themselves on demand.

hyperframes.blurb: HeyGen HyperFrames 0.7.x — render HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4; `check` is the verification gate; pinned Chrome at /etc/sl8/chrome-path; media via ai-gen.

hyperframes-suite.blurb: The studio's locked skill suite baked in: /hyperframes router, motion-graphics workflow, and the 8 domain skills — sessions start instantly, no installs. Other workflows lazy-install on route.

fonts.blurb: Embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) plus DejaVu/Comic-Neue — the offline-closure font set.

chrome-headless.blurb: Headless-Chrome system libraries for the renderer.

There is NO router and NO workflow skill in the image: this is a DERIVATION runtime — the bot definition's skills list (botSkills) supplies the workflow(s) this bot runs, installed at provisioning; start every request from the bot's own INDEX.md/setup.md front door and the workflow(s) it names. STEP DISCIPLINE (non-negotiable): follow the workflow's numbered steps exactly — dispatch sub-agents where the runbook says dispatch, leave every step's artifact on disk, and run the snapshot proof BEFORE render. PROJECT ROOT: map the workflow's PROJECT_DIR under /home/user/artifacts/<project>/ (one folder per project). The hyperframes CLI npx cache is pre-warmed: render via the project-pinned form (`npx --yes hyperframes@<pinned> render ...`). OFFLINE CLOSURE: strip Google Fonts links (0.8.x still auto-fetches; a closed sandbox turns that into FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE, i.e. a FAILED render), map families to the packed fonts (Inter/Outfit/Fraunces/Anton/Space Grotesk), declare `@font-face { src: local('X') }` INSIDE each composition's [data-composition-id] wrapper; closure oracle = `check` exit 0 with zero 'Fetched ... from Google Fonts' compiler lines. AUDIO: mixing already-placed audio (fades, crossfade, gain, ducking, voiceover carve, FX, automation envelopes) is `hyperframes-audio` — new at the 0.8.8 refresh; sourcing or generating audio remains media-use.

ui.tagline: The HyperFrames derivation runtime — the core craft baked, your bot brings its own workflows.
ui.description: The hyperframes-studio DERIVATION runtime for specialist bots: the 13-skill core tier is pre-installed (animation, keyframes, creative direction, CLI, registry, media, Figma import, and the 5-skill motion-quality doctrine chain), plus the HyperFrames 0.7.x renderer, a pinned offline Chrome, fonts, ffmpeg, and Python. No router and no workflow skills in the image — a bot built on this template declares exactly the workflows its persona needs in its own skills list, and they install at provisioning. Built for Market persona bots derived from hyperframes-studio releases; for the full ready-to-work studio, use the HyperFrames template instead.

hyperframes.blurb: HeyGen HyperFrames 0.7.x — render HTML/CSS/GSAP compositions to MP4; `check` is the verification gate; pinned Chrome at /etc/sl8/chrome-path; media via ai-gen.

hyperframes-suite-core.blurb: The studio's CORE tier baked in: 8 domain skills + the 5-skill doctrine chain — no router, no workflows. The bot's own skills list supplies its workflows at provisioning.

fonts.blurb: Embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) plus DejaVu/Comic-Neue — the offline-closure font set.

chrome-headless.blurb: Headless-Chrome system libraries for the renderer.

ffmpeg.blurb: Encode and convert video and audio.

packs.description: Python 3 + pip + venv + build tooling for native extensions.
packs.agentGuidance: Python 3 is at `python3` (no unversioned `python`). Use `pip3 install --break-system-packages <pkg>` for system-wide installs (this image follows PEP 668), or `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` for a project-local venv. Native-extension build tools (build-essential, pkg-config, python3-dev) are present, so packages like Pillow, lxml, manim can compile from source if needed.

packs.description: FFmpeg for video/audio encoding and frame-to-MP4 assembly.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `ffmpeg -i <input> <output>` for transcoding, `ffmpeg -framerate <fps> -i frame_%04d.png out.mp4` for frame sequences, and `ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>` to inspect media. The Debian ffmpeg build includes the common codecs (libx264, libvpx, aac); use `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for broadly-compatible MP4 output.

packs.description: Curated font set for caption/composition rendering: DejaVu family (Sans, Sans Oblique, Serif Italic at guaranteed paths) + Comic Neue (OFL casual), plus an embeddable OFL webfont pack (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) for legible, consistent HyperFrames/video compositions. fontconfig (fc-list/fc-match) for discovery.
packs.agentGuidance: Fonts are pre-installed — do NOT probe the filesystem or fetch fonts at runtime. Guaranteed TTF paths for ffmpeg drawtext fontfile=: /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (clean sans, default), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Oblique.ttf (sans oblique), /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSerif-Italic.ttf (serif italic). Casual/handwriting: Comic Neue (OFL; resolve with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Comic Neue'`). Embeddable webfonts for compositions (HyperFrames HTML/CSS or ffmpeg drawtext font='...'): Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk — installed under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/sl8-webfonts and registered with fontconfig, so reference by family name (e.g. `font='Inter'`) or resolve a file with `fc-match -f '%{file}' 'Outfit'`. `fc-list` enumerates everything installed. ffmpeg's drawtext is built with fontconfig, so family names work as an alternative to fontfile=.

packs.description: ImageMagick 6 (convert, identify, montage, mogrify) for raster image manipulation and animated GIF assembly from PNG frames.
packs.agentGuidance: Debian ships the ImageMagick 6.x series: the entry point is `convert` (plus `identify`, `montage`, `mogrify`) — there is NO `magick` binary, do not call it. Assemble animated GIFs from PNG frames with `convert -delay 20 -loop 0 frame-*.png out.gif` (delay is in 1/100ths of a second; -loop 0 = infinite). Inspect images with `identify <file>` (one line per GIF frame). Raster formats (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) are unrestricted; the default security policy only limits ghostscript-backed coders like PDF/PS.

packs.description: jq — command-line JSON processor for parsing and transforming JSON in shell pipelines.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `jq` to parse JSON in shell scripts — e.g. `ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams in.mp4 | jq -r '.format.duration'`. `-e` makes the exit code follow the filter's truthiness (use it for assertions); `-r` prints raw strings without quotes. `sl8-capabilities | jq '.packs[].id'` lists this sandbox's installed packs.

packs.description: Bakes the video-studio skill suite (locked registry pins: the explainer-video and cinematic-video workflows + the five domain skills) into /home/user/.claude/skills — the studio template rule: sessions never re-install what every session needs. Suite source of truth: the release lockfile (studio/video-studio/releases/vN/suite.lock.json). Requires a GITHUB_TOKEN build env (registry read); blanked from the image ENV after install.
packs.agentGuidance: The video-studio suite is PRE-INSTALLED at /home/user/.claude/skills. TWO creation workflows, and the brief decides which: a NARRATED explainer (script + voiceover, boards-first) starts at explainer-video; a CHARACTER piece with a locked identity and NO narration (story, scene, action) starts at cinematic-video. There is no router yet — pick by the brief and follow that workflow's numbered steps EXACTLY. Common law across both: the plan JSON is approved before any paid call; style.md before any frame; every frame APPROVED before any motion spend (re-roll stills, ~25x cheaper than clips); QC input gates before assembly; frame-extraction + contact sheet before any delivery claim. explainer-video adds: every VO take MEASURED before any duration is set (visuals stretch to audio, never the reverse). cinematic-video adds: the frozen CHARACTER_BLOCK is reused VERBATIM in every shot prompt (a paraphrase IS identity drift), engine-native audio only, and no dialogue or on-screen text anywhere. Every step's artifact lands under /home/user/artifacts/<project>/ — a run missing a step artifact is a failed run regardless of the MP4. PAID CALLS: ai-gen only, and the contract has ONE home — video-prompting/SKILL.md 'Paid-call contract' (validate, estimate, one call at a time under --max-cost, journal request ids, account by balance delta and NEVER credits_used) including the charged-vs-uncharged failure table (422/7/13/10). Read assembly-qc/references/models-and-gotchas.md BEFORE debugging any failure — most failures are documented.

ui.tagline: Cutting, encoding and captioning — for Specialists who ship video.
ui.description: Everything in General, plus a local video-assembly toolchain: ffmpeg/ffprobe with the full normalize-concat-caption feature set (zoompan, drawtext, concat demuxer, anoisesrc/amix audio beds), ImageMagick for animated GIF assembly, a curated caption-font set (DejaVu family + Comic Neue at guaranteed paths), jq, and Python 3.11. Generation stays remote via ai-gen — pick this when a bot needs to cut, normalize, caption, and package clips into finished MP4s.

ffmpeg.blurb: Cut, normalize, caption, and stitch clips into finished MP4s.

imagemagick.blurb: Assemble PNG frames into animated GIFs and inspect or convert images.

fonts.blurb: DejaVu + Comic Neue + embeddable webfonts (Inter, Outfit, Fraunces, Anton, Space Grotesk) at known paths, ready for caption cards.

jq.blurb: Parse and transform JSON right in the shell.

python-runtime.blurb: Python 3.11 with pip and venv for scripting and data wrangling.
